title: Arbitrary scalar extension of the flat curve cofactor map
statement:
Let $R$ be a commutative ring, $c\geq0$, $P=R[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$, and $I=(f_1,\ldots,f_c)$ for an ordered regular sequence [def-weil-pbc-regular-sequence]. Put $B=P/I$, $C=I/I^2$, $V=\bigoplus_{j=0}^c B\,dx_j$ and $u:C\to V$, $u(\bar f_i)=\sum_j\overline{\partial f_i/\partial x_j}dx_j$. Differentials mean [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], and exterior powers mean [def-weil-pbc-exterior-algebra]. Write $E=[C\xrightarrow{u}V]$ in degrees $-1,0$ and $D(E)=(\bigwedge^c C)^\vee\otimes_B\bigwedge^{c+1}V$, with $M^\vee=\operatorname{Hom}_B(M,B)$. Assume that $B$ is flat over $R$ [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]. For any ring homomorphism $R\to R'$, put $P'=R'[x_0,\ldots,x_c]$, let $f'_i$ be the coefficient images of $f_i$, and put $I'=(f'_1,\ldots,f'_c)$, $B'=P'/I'=B\otimes_RR'$, $C'=I'/I'^2$ and $V'=\bigoplus_j B'\,dx_j$. Let $E'=[C'\xrightarrow{df'}V']$ and $D(E')=(\bigwedge^c C')^\vee\otimes_{B'}\bigwedge^{c+1}V'$. There are canonical isomorphisms $C\otimes_BB'\simeq C'$, $V\otimes_BB'\simeq V'$ sending equation classes and coordinate differentials to their primed counterparts. Write $L_{B/R}$ and $L_{B'/R'}$ for the cotangent complexes of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation], and $E\simeq L_{B/R}$ for the conormal comparison of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]. The comparison
$$E\otimes_BB'\simeq L_{B/R}\otimes_B^{\mathbf L}B'\simeq L_{B'/R'}$$
is an isomorphism in the derived category and identifies its displayed two-term model with $E'$, with degree-zero map the isomorphism $\eta:\Omega^1_{B/R}\otimes_BB'\simeq\Omega^1_{B'/R'}$, $d\bar x_j\otimes1\mapsto d\bar x'_j$. Use the determinant functor of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] and the local wedge map $w$ of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]. The primed wedge formula defines $w':\Omega^1_{B'/R'}\to D(E')$, and the induced determinant comparison $\delta:D(E)\otimes_BB'\simeq D(E')$ satisfies
$$\delta\circ(w\otimes_BB')=w'\circ\eta.$$
The map $\delta$ sends $\bigl((\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c)^\vee\otimes(dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c)\bigr)\otimes1$ to $(\bar f'_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f'_c)^\vee\otimes(dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c)$. Thus the augmented Jacobian formulas also commute with coefficient extension. These comparisons commute with affine localization, transport by isomorphisms, identity ring maps and composition $R\to R'\to R''$, including composition of the intrinsic cotangent and determinant comparisons. No Noetherian or flatness hypothesis on $R'$ or $R\to R'$ is imposed; the primed wedge formula uses the displayed conormal basis and does not require globally regular equations over $P'$.

proof.text: Use [lem-weil-pbc-polynomial-scalar-extension] and [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-quotient-base-change] to identify $P\otimes_RR'=P'$ and $B\otimes_RR'=B'$, by coefficient extension. Tensor $0\to I\to P\to B\to0$ over $R$ with $R'$. Since its last term $B$ is $R$-flat, [lem-weil-pbc-flat-quotient-tensor-injective] identifies $I\otimes_RR'$ with the kernel $I'$ of $P'\to B'$, sending $a\otimes r'$ to $r'a'$. This uses flatness of the quotient, not of the scalar extension.

Apply [lem-weil-pbc-tensor-right-exact] to $I^2\to I\to C\to0$. Under step 1 the image of $I^2\otimes_RR'$ in $I'$ is exactly $I'^2$: a product $(\sum a_k\otimes r_k)(\sum b_l\otimes s_l)$ is $\sum a_kb_l\otimes r_ks_l$, and conversely $ab\otimes r'=(a\otimes1)(b\otimes r')$. Thus $C\otimes_RR'\simeq I'/I'^2$. By the tensor universal property [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product], $C\otimes_B(B\otimes_RR')\simeq C\otimes_RR'$ via $z\otimes(b\otimes r')\mapsto bz\otimes r'$, with inverse $z\otimes r'\mapsto z\otimes(1\otimes r')$. This proves the asserted canonical conormal isomorphism and its equation-class formula.

source.place: Tag 00DF (lemma-tensor-product-exact), applied to the square-ideal quotient; elementary multiplication and tensor balancing

proof.text:
The conormal basis and the cokernel description of $\Omega^1_{B/R}$ come from [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]. Scalar extension sends the two displayed free bases to bases over $B'$: identify a free module with a finite direct sum and send each coordinate tensor to its product in $B'$, with inverse $\sum b'_je_j\mapsto\sum e_j\otimes b'_j$ [def-weil-pbc-module-tensor-product]. Step 2 therefore supplies the basis of $C'$ without assuming regularity of the primed equations. The coordinate map similarly identifies $V\otimes_BB'$ with $V'$. For a monomial $a x^
u$, coefficient extension commutes with $\partial/\partial x_j$, since both orders give $
u_j a' x^{
u-e_j}$; add over its finitely many monomials. Consequently the matrix of $u\otimes1$ is $df'$. Tensor right exactness identifies its cokernel with $\Omega^1_{B/R}\otimes_BB'$. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change], this is canonically $\Omega^1_{B'/R'}$ through $d ar x_j\otimes1\mapsto d ar x'_j$; this is $\eta$.

source.place: Tag 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change), Tag 00DF; coefficientwise differentiation and free-module tensor calculation

proof.text: The complex $B[0]$ is K-flat over $R$, by [lem-pc-module-bounded-flat-kflat], and [lem-pc-source-kflat-module-tensor-model] computes $B[0]\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}R'[0]$ as $(B\otimes_RR')[0]=B'[0]$. Thus this square is Tor-independent. The complex $E$ has finite free $B$-terms by [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization], hence is K-flat by the same theorem; its ordinary tensor with $B'$ computes its derived tensor. Apply the Tor-independent base-change clause of [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation] to $\operatorname{Spec}B\to\operatorname{Spec}R$. It gives the asserted derived isomorphism. That node also states compatibility with the local conormal models, so steps 2 and 3 identify its model with $E'$ and its $H^0$ map with $\eta$. We have not applied the regular-presentation theorem to possibly nonregular global equations in $P'$.

Apply the pullback and model comparisons of [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] to step 4. Their affine expression is the tensor of the top exterior and dual comparisons in [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons], followed by the conormal and coordinate isomorphisms. Both terms are finite free, so these comparisons apply to $C,V$ and to $\bigwedge^c C$. Write $e=\bar f_1\wedge\cdots\wedge\bar f_c$ and $v_0=dx_0\wedge\cdots\wedge dx_c$, and put primes on their images. The exterior maps send $e\otimes1$ to $e'$ and $v_0\otimes1$ to $v'_0$; the dual comparison sends $e^\vee\otimes1$ to the functional taking $e'$ to $1$, namely $e'^\vee$. Thus the induced map $\delta$ sends $(e^\vee\otimes v_0)\otimes1$ to $e'^\vee\otimes v'_0$, with the relation-first orientation unchanged.

source.place: Tag 0FJY (remark-functorial-det); more-algebra.tex Tags 0FJ9 and 0FJB, exterior and dual scalar comparisons

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent] to $u':C'\to V'$ (the free modules of step 3). It gives a well-defined map on $\operatorname{coker}u'=\Omega^1_{B'/R'}$ by the primed wedge formula, even when $u'$ is not injective. This is $w'$. For a lift $v\in V$ of $\omega\in\Omega^1_{B/R}$, let $v'$ denote its image in $V'$. The formula of [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization] and the exterior/dual maps of step 5 give
$$\delta(w(\omega)\otimes1)=e'^\vee\otimes(u'(\bar f'_1)\wedge\cdots\wedge u'(\bar f'_c)\wedge v')=w'(\eta(\omega\otimes1)).$$
The elements $\omega\otimes1$ generate over $B'$, so the required square commutes. In the indicated trivializations the coefficient of $v'_0$ is the determinant of the primed augmented Jacobian: expand the wedge multilinearly over permutations of the $dx_j$. Step 3 identifies every entry with its coefficient image, and the finite permutation sum for the determinant commutes with a ring homomorphism. This proves the augmented Jacobian assertion as well.

source.place: Tag 0E9Y (lemma-determinant), displayed wedge formula; primed well-definedness supplied by the cited arbitrary-differential cofactor construction

proof.text: For $R\to R'\to R''$, all ordinary comparisons agree on $\bar f_i$, $dx_j$, $d\bar x_j$ and $e^\vee\otimes v_0$: either route sends each to its double-primed counterpart, and these generate their modules. The same calculation gives the identity law. The intrinsic derived cotangent maps have identity, composition and local-model compatibility by [lem-trf-lci-cotangent-presentation]; the determinant pullback maps have these laws and are natural for derived isomorphisms by [lem-trf-two-term-perfect-determinant] and [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons]. For localization, [lem-weil-pbc-localization-module-exact] identifies localized conormal quotients and cokernels, and [lem-weil-pbc-localization-tensor-product] identifies localized scalar tensors; exterior/dual maps and wedge maps localize by [lem-trf-projective-exterior-scalar-comparisons] and [lem-sfb-cofactor-local-descent]. Their formulas on fractions are the same formulas with localized coefficients. Finally the conormal realization is compatible with transport by isomorphisms by [lem-sfb-affine-conormal-jacobian-realization]; [lem-sfb-two-term-cofactor-naturality] identifies the wedge maps under the resulting derived comparisons, including changes of two-term model. These naturality statements make the coefficient-extension square compatible with such transport. Empty wedges and $\bigwedge^0 C=B$ give the asserted $c=0$ case, and the formulas remain valid if $B'=0$.
